packages.title: EPC lodgement versus operational emissions QA
facts: EPC statistics are based on certificates lodged on the Energy Performance of Buildings Registers.
The live tables include ratings, modelled energy use, carbon-dioxide indicators, costs and floor area.
Certificate metrics are assessment outputs and do not necessarily equal subsequent metered operational energy use.
A building may have multiple certificates over time.
Certificate data must not be treated as a live parcel emissions monitor.

packages.title: EPC local-authority allocation revision QA
facts: MHCLG revised EPC live tables in May 2026 following a processing error allocating a minority of EPCs to some old local-authority areas.
The department described the overall impact as small.
Corrected local-authority allocation should supersede the affected earlier tables.
A location-processing correction can affect local counts without changing the underlying certificate assessment.
Revision history is retained in QA rather than silently ignored.

packages.title: EPC weekly-table revision boundary QA
facts: MHCLG states the weekly EPC live table was unaffected by the May 2026 local-authority processing correction.
The revision applied to affected live tables but did not imply every EPC product was wrong.
Revision scope must be preserved by table rather than generalized to the whole collection.
Weekly counts remain certificate-lodgement indicators.
No operational emissions value is inferred from revision status.

packages.title: Public-building DEC data-quality caution QA
facts: The public-building DEC dataset describes roughly 40,000 public buildings over 1,000 square metres in England and Wales.
The dataset includes energy, floorspace, emissions and efficiency-rating fields.
Its metadata warns that data-entry or collection errors can produce incorrect ratings, including cases with missing kWh or CO2 data.
A DEC dataset is not complete coverage of every building or parcel.
Data-quality flags must be reviewed before any site-level use.

packages.title: GBIS 139,100 measures-installed QA
facts: DESNZ reports 139,100 GBIS measures installed from scheme start to the end of March 2026.
The June 2026 release is based on provisional Ofgem data.
Measure counts are based on completed installation dates recorded in the Ofgem register.
A measure count is not a measured energy saving or greenhouse-gas reduction.
No parcel emissions saving is inferred from the installation count alone.

packages.title: GBIS 100,900 households-upgraded QA
facts: DESNZ reports 100,900 households upgraded under GBIS to the end of March 2026.
Household count and measure count are distinct because a household can receive more than one measure.
The figures cover Great Britain rather than the entire United Kingdom.
A household-upgrade count does not establish realised household energy savings.
No cadastral parcel value is assigned from scheme totals.

packages.title: GBIS provisional-revision QA
facts: DESNZ states GBIS Ofgem data in the June 2026 release remain provisional and subject to revision.
The June release includes minor revisions to end-March measure delivery compared with the prior release.
DESNZ anticipates at least one further release later in 2026 to cover final revisions.
Provisional administrative counts must retain their revision status.
No provisional measure total is converted into parcel emissions.

packages.title: Ofgem ECO submitted-measures scope QA
facts: Ofgem's ECO public data page reports measures submitted to Ofgem as of 7 July 2026.
The table separates measure types and scheme phases including ECO4.
A submitted administrative measure record is not itself a greenhouse-gas measurement.
Measure-type counts do not establish realised energy savings without the relevant scheme methodology.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from submitted-measure counts.

packages.title: Ofgem ECO exemption-measure exclusion QA
facts: Ofgem states its displayed measure table excludes ECO4 measures notified as exemption measures.
The exclusion changes the coverage of the administrative count.
Excluded records must not be silently treated as zero activity.
Coverage notes are required when comparing ECO tables with other scheme statistics.
No emissions inference is made from the exclusion.

packages.title: Supplier non-compliance versus emissions QA
facts: Ofgem's Supplier Performance Report covers non-compliance incidents from 1 July to 31 December 2025.
The report spans environmental and social schemes including ECO and GBIS.
Incident counts measure regulatory or delivery compliance rather than physical emissions.
A supplier's number of incidents does not state its energy sales or greenhouse-gas footprint.
No site or parcel GHG value is inferred from compliance incidents.

packages.title: Non-Domestic RHI Q1-2026 scheme-update QA
facts: Ofgem Non-Domestic RHI Quarterly Report Issue 57 covers 1 January to 31 March 2026.
The scheme supports uptake of renewable and low-carbon heat.
Quarterly scheme reporting describes programme delivery and participation rather than direct stack-emissions measurements.
Technology or accreditation records do not by themselves establish realised carbon savings.
No parcel emissions value is inferred without verified installation activity and geometry.

packages.title: 2026 conversion-factors activity-versus-spend QA
facts: DESNZ published the 2026 greenhouse-gas reporting conversion factors on 11 June 2026.
The activity-based factors differ from Defra spend-based emissions multipliers used with carbon-footprint data.
DESNZ notes spend-based methods can provide an initial supply-chain assessment when sufficient activity data are unavailable.
Users should report the methods used in their emissions accounting.
A conversion factor alone is not an observed parcel emission; compatible activity data are required.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel-inference guard 105 QA
facts: The reviewed sources mix national accounts, local models, monitoring concentrations, administrative schemes, waste activity, water restrictions and certificate data.
Their geographic units range from UK and Great Britain to England, local authorities, monitoring sites and scheme records.
Their quantities include CO2e, energy, tax revenue, concentrations, waste mass, counts, percentages and regulatory thresholds.
Cross-source arithmetic is forbidden unless accounting basis, year, geography, unit and methodology are compatible.
No reviewed source establishes a verified cadastral parcel binding, so parcel emissions remain unproduced.
